title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
question: After subtracting stock-based compensation, $1.5B in UK VAT cash outflows, and $10.65B in net pending M&A outlays, what FCF growth does $63.47 actually price in?

epigraph.quote: Headline cash flow flatters companies that pay engineers in stock and buy growth with debt. True underwriting starts only after you deduct both.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $63.47 (TradingView: $63.48), Uber carries a $129.60 billion market cap and a $137.96 billion headline enterprise value [1, 21, 31]. Trailing twelve-month Free Cash Flow reached $10,421 million ($10.42 billion) through Q3 2026 [3, 32]. On headline ratios, shares trade at 12.44x P/FCF, 14.51x forward earnings, 15.81x EV/EBITDA, and 2.44x EV/Sales [21]. Yet those surface multiples miss three major cash and debt adjustments from the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q [31].

Forensic Cash Flow & EV Normalization: First, stock-based compensation (SBC) totaled $1,614 million in 9M 2026, or $2,152 million annualized [31]. Deducting $2.15 billion of real dilution from $10.42 billion of TTM FCF yields $8.27 billion in standalone SBC-adjusted FCF. Second, Uber holds $10,068 million in unrestricted cash and short-term investments [31]. Another $11,372 million in restricted cash and investments stays locked against $13,709 million in injury reserves [31]. Against $15,664 million in long-term debt (+49% from year-end 2025) and $2,073 million in operating leases, current net debt and leases stand at $7.67 billion [31]. Third, Uber faces $1.50 billion in pending UK HMRC back-VAT cash outflows [31]. Pending M&A adds ~$10.65 billion in net cash or debt costs ($2.30 billion for ezCater plus ~$8.35 billion net for Delivery Hero after existing stakes, swaps, and carve-outs) [31, 33].

Those adjustments lift Uber's real valuation hurdle. Adding $7.67 billion of net debt and leases plus $1.50 billion of UK VAT cash gives $9.17 billion in standalone obligations. That produces a $138.60 billion standalone EV, or 16.76x standalone SBC-adjusted FCF (a 6.0% yield, versus 12.44x headline P/FCF). On a pro-forma basis, total net debt and deal costs reach $19.82 billion ($149.25 billion EV). Crediting $0.45 billion in conservative initial M&A cash flow ($8.72 billion pro-forma FCF) puts shares at 17.12x normalized EV/(FCF - SBC) [31, 33].

Why has the stock fallen 31.59% from its $92.78 52-week high? Investors are pricing two shocks: autonomous vehicle (AV) risk and a sudden M&A pivot [31, 32]. Waymo now runs its own ride-hailing app alongside Uber, while Tesla and Zoox scale closed-loop fleets [18, 22, 31]. At the same time, quarterly buybacks dropped 75% from $3,010 million in Q1 to $754 million in Q3 as cash shifted into Delivery Hero, ezCater, SpotHero, Getir, and Blacklane [31].

web_blocks.caption: Reverse DCF & Scenario Valuation Matrix at $63.47 CMP (SBC-Adjusted Pro-Forma EV: $149.25B; Normalized FCF: $8.72B)
web_blocks.takeaway: After deducting $2.15B SBC, $7.67B net debt, $1.50B UK VAT cash, and $10.65B deal outlays, $63.47 implies 5.59%–7.00% 10Y growth [31, 33]. Stripping +$0.45B unclosed M&A FCF drops Base to $70.14 ($65.50 after -$0.48B drag), while adding the $2.34B insurance reserve gap cuts Bear to $41.78.

web_blocks.html: Standalone & Combined Stress Sensitivity: Crediting +$0.45 billion of unclosed M&A cash flow flatters Base fair value to $75.00. Stripping that +$0.45 billion credit alone ($8.27 billion standalone FCF) drops Base fair value to $70.14 per share (+10.5% vs. $63.47, below our $72.60 expected value). Deducting -$0.48 billion for incremental Euro/M&A interest and recurring legal reserves ($7.79 billion FCF) lowers standalone value further to $65.50 per share (+3.2%). In a combined Bear stress—starting from $7.77 billion FCF (-$0.50 billion interest/tax/regulatory drag), slowing 10-year CAGR to 4.0% at 10.5% WACC and 2.0% terminal growth, and adding the $2.34 billion uncollateralized insurance reserve gap ($13,709M total reserves less $11,372M restricted cash/investments = $22.16B total deduction)—equity fair value falls to $41.78 per share (-34.2%) [31]. Re-weighting to 45% Stressed Bear ($41.78), 45% Standalone Base ($70.14), and 10% Bull ($108.00) yields a stressed expected value of $61.16 per share (-3.6% vs. CMP).

web_blocks.the_number: $75.00 per share Base Case fair value (vs. $63.47 CMP, $45.00 Bear, and $108.00 Bull). Expected 12-month value is $72.60.
web_blocks.how_calculated: We run a 10-year cash flow model starting from $8.72B of pro-forma SBC-adjusted FCF. We discount at a 10.0% WACC with 2.5% terminal growth, then deduct $19.82B of net debt, leases, UK VAT cash, and deal costs across 2,039.3M shares.
web_blocks.the_inputs: Base FCF uses $10.42B TTM FCF less $2.15B SBC plus $0.45B net M&A cash flow. Key rates use 7.5% 10Y growth, 5.04% 10Y Treasury yield [23], and 1.27 beta [21]. Debt adjustments total $19.82B [31].
web_blocks.the_range: Primary scenarios span $45.00 Bear (3.0% growth, 10.5% WACC, 2.0% g) to $108.00 Bull (10.5% growth, 9.5% WACC, 3.0% g), yielding $72.60 EV (+14.4%). Stripping unclosed M&A FCF cuts Base to $70.14 ($65.50 with -$0.48B drag), while combined Bear stress with the $2.34B insurance gap yields $41.78 (-34.2%).
web_blocks.if_off: If unclosed M&A fails to add FCF, recurring debt/legal drag trims $0.50B/yr, Waymo/Tesla cap CAGR at 4%, and the $2.34B uncollateralized insurance gap enters net debt, fair value drops to $41.78 (-34.2%).

web_blocks.caption: Uber vs. Listed Mobility, Delivery & Autonomous Peers (Session Cutoff: 2026-11-20)
web_blocks.takeaway: Uber trades at 14.51x forward P/E and 12.44x headline P/FCF (17.12x normalized EV/(FCF-SBC)). That sits below DoorDash at 32.07x forward P/E and Alphabet at 17.73x forward P/E [21, 31].

web_blocks.html: Cross-sectional peer checks frame Uber's discount honestly [21]. DoorDash ($66.53B market cap) grows sales faster (+35.03% YoY), yet posts a 6.18% operating margin and trades at 32.07x forward P/E and 30.20x P/FCF. Both Uber and DoorDash sit in Stage 4. Lyft ($6.23B market cap) trades at 5.52x P/FCF and 0.81x EV/Sales on a -2.25% operating margin, yet holds Stage 2 at $16.48. Alphabet (GOOGL, Waymo's parent) trades at $265.29 (17.73x forward P/E, 33.33% operating margin, +22.21% sales growth). Investors can own the top AV builder directly without taking on Delivery Hero integration risk.

web_blocks.mechanism: Existential platform-disruption fears (Apple ATT privacy changes plus TikTok competition) collided with heavy capital spending (Reality Labs) to compress Meta's cash multiple to ~10x FCF before management halted capex bloat and restored buybacks.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Meta shares fell 76% from $382 (Sep 2021) to $88 (Nov 2022) at ~9.5x forward P/E before cost discipline doubled FCF from $19B (2022) to $44B (2023) and sparked a >450% rebound.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Cheap cash multiples alone do not arrest a Stage 4 markdown while capital spending is accelerating; re-rating begins only when management caps empire-building outlays and proves core take rates are intact.

web_blocks.html: What Changes Our Valuation View: Our $75.00 Base valuation assumes 7.5% normalized 10-year FCF compounding and <2.0x post-M&A net leverage. Further Delivery Hero dilution, UK/EU antitrust remedies, or Mobility take-rate compression below 23% would push fair value toward $45.00.

book_paragraphs: Now that we have updated Uber's operating and balance-sheet ledger without looking at the stock price, let us open the November 20, 2026 market quote and run the numbers cleanly. At $63.47 per share ($63.48 on TradingView), Uber carries a market capitalization of $129.60 billion and a headline enterprise value of $137.96 billion. On the surface, trailing twelve-month Free Cash Flow of $10.42 billion makes the stock look dirt cheap at 12.44 times P/FCF and 14.51 times forward earnings. Yet Pass 1 taught us that headline cash flow flatters any business that issues billions in stock compensation and has $12 billion of off-model cash outlays queued up.

Let us strip out the flattery step by step so we see the true owner yield. First, Uber recorded $1,614 million of stock-based compensation in the first nine months of 2026, or $2,152 million annualized. Deducting that $2.15 billion dilution cost from $10.42 billion of trailing FCF leaves $8.27 billion of true standalone SBC-adjusted Free Cash Flow. Second, look at the September 30, 2026 balance sheet: Uber holds $10,068 million in unrestricted cash and short-term investments, while its $11,372 million of restricted cash and investments stays legally locked inside its captive insurance arm against $13,709 million in injury reserves. Measuring $15,664 million of long-term debt and $2,073 million of operating leases against unrestricted liquidity produces $7.67 billion of net debt and leases. Third, add the $1.50 billion remaining UK HMRC back-VAT appeal payment and roughly $10.65 billion in net pending M&A outlays—$2.30 billion for ezCater plus $8.35 billion net for Delivery Hero after accounting for Uber's $3.37 billion existing equity stake, $1.48 billion total return swap, and $1.60 billion SSW Partners carve-out.

When you put all of those pieces together, pro-forma net debt and cash commitments reach $19.82 billion, lifting Uber's pro-forma enterprise value to $149.25 billion. Even crediting ezCater and Delivery Hero with $0.45 billion of conservative initial net FCF ($8.72 billion pro-forma SBC-adjusted FCF), Uber actually trades at 17.12 times normalized EV-to-FCF—not 12.4 times. That is still reasonable for a dual-engine marketplace, yet it is far from a distressed giveaway once leverage and integration risk enter the frame.

A clean 10-year Reverse DCF confirms what $63.47 prices in today. Using our pro-forma $8.72 billion SBC-adjusted FCF base, a 10.0% WACC (reflecting a 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield, 1.27 equity beta, and M&A execution risk), and a 2.5% terminal growth rate, today's enterprise value implies a 5.59% 10-year FCF growth rate—rising to 7.00% if we apply a stricter 10.5% WACC and 2.0% terminal growth rate. Notice how different that picture is from prior assumptions: the market is no longer pricing zero growth on an unencumbered cash cow, but rather mid-single-digit normalized compounding weighed down by autonomous disruption and heavy M&A.

Underwriting our scenarios on that same normalized math sets clear value boundaries. In our Base case (50% probability), normalized FCF compounds at 7.5% over a decade at a 10.0% WACC and 2.5% terminal growth, yielding $75.00 per share (+18.2% above CMP). In our Bear case (30% probability), autonomous disintermediation by Waymo and Tesla alongside Delivery Hero integration drag slows FCF growth to 3.0% at a 10.5% WACC, cutting fair value to $45.00 (-29.1%). In our Bull case (20% probability), Uber proves indispensable as the hybrid AV demand aggregator while M&A synergies lift FCF growth to 10.5% at a 9.5% WACC, valuing shares at $108.00 (+70.2%). Weighting all three yields a 12-month expected value of $72.60.

We must also stress-test our Base and Bear numbers without crediting unclosed M&A synergies upfront. Stripping the +$0.45 billion M&A cash flow credit alone drops standalone Base fair value from $75.00 to $70.14 per share (+10.5% vs. $63.47), and deducting -$0.48 billion for incremental debt interest and legal reserves trims standalone value to $65.50 (+3.2%). Worse, if we combine -$0.50 billion of interest and regulatory drag ($7.77 billion FCF_0), a 4.0% ten-year CAGR, a 10.5% WACC, 2.0% terminal growth, and the $2.34 billion uncollateralized insurance reserve deficit ($13,709 million total reserves minus $11,372 million restricted cash, lifting net deductions to $22.16 billion), combined Bear fair value falls to $41.78 per share (-34.2%). Re-weighting to 45% Stressed Bear ($41.78), 45% Standalone Base ($70.14), and 10% Bull ($108.00) cuts 12-month expected value to $61.16 per share (-3.6% below current price).

Compare Uber against its live November 20, 2026 peer group and the tension becomes obvious. DoorDash ($66.53 billion market cap) grows top-line revenue at 35.03%, yet converts only 6.18% into operating margin and trades at 32.07 times forward earnings. Lyft ($6.23 billion market cap) trades at 5.52 times P/FCF with negative 2.25% operating margins, though it sits in Stage 2 momentum. Most tellingly, Alphabet—Waymo's parent—trades at $265.29, or 17.73 times forward earnings with 33.33% operating margins and 22.21% revenue growth. Like Meta Platforms in late 2022 when spending fears crushed its multiple, Uber's valuation upside will stay trapped until management proves M&A discipline and protects core take rates.

To stress-test what changes our valuation model, track three quarterly signals. First, watch whether the Delivery Hero closing preserves net leverage below 2.0 times Adjusted EBITDA without forcing additional equity dilution or high-coupon Euro debt. Second, track whether Mobility take rates hold above 23% as Waymo scales past 700 autonomous vehicles in late 2026 and 2,000 in 2027. Third, monitor UK HMRC appeal cash outflows and Australian payroll tax accruals so operating cash flow conversion stays intact.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: THE REAL MULTIPLE AFTER SBC AND M&A
book_callouts.text: On headline numbers, Uber trades at 12.44 times free cash flow. Once you subtract $2.15 billion in annual stock-based compensation, $1.50 billion in pending UK VAT cash outflows, and $10.65 billion in net Delivery Hero and ezCater outlays, the true normalized multiple rises to 17.1 times. Good analysis never uses flattering denominators.
